title: Plugin marketplace revamp
subtitle: One structured entry for skills, experts, and expert teams. This brief leads with the decisions, then scope, impact, and acceptance.

items.title: One template structure
items.text: The registry keeps a single skill structure; user uploads and official listings share it.

items.title: Teams get uploads
items.text: Compose a team prompt from marketplace experts and name one member as leader.

items.title: Fixed creation order
items.text: Skill first, then expert, then team; the order never reverses.

items.title: Signed listings
items.text: Every published plugin is content-signed at review time.

items.title: One-click rollback
items.text: Any release can roll back to the last signed version in one click.

items.title: Usage analytics
items.text: Authors see installs, retention, and failure counts per version.

items.label: Submit
items.text: Author uploads the manifest and bundle.

items.label: Review
items.text: Automated checks plus a human pass.

items.label: Sign
items.text: The signing service pins content hashes.

cells: Re-upload the full bundle per release

sections.title: Risks and dependencies
sections.text: The signing service ships two weeks before the marketplace cutover. If the key-management integration slips, R4 falls back to hash pinning and keeps the release date.

items.text: A new author publishes a signed plugin without leaving the wizard

Search returns a plugin by capability, not only by name

footer: R1–R3 product, R4–R5 platform, R6 growth. Security sign-off is required before R4 enters build. All names and figures are synthetic sample data.
